Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. India are in the huddle before they stride out to the middle. Sidra Ameen and Javeria Khan are the openers. Jhulan Goswami has the ball...
... The Chase...

Right then! 245 to win for Pakistan Women. The pitch looks good to bat on and Pakistan do have some ranks in their batting while India possesses power in their bowling. A very interesting second half coming up. Stay tuned...

Nida Dar is up for a quick chat. She says that she didn't start well but managed to come back well in her next spell. Tells that she wanted to bowl according to the situation and she is happy in the end. Mentions that 244 is a good score but it is also a good pitch to bat on and they will fancy their chances going into the chase. Says that they have some quality batters in their ranks and they are confident of chasing the total down.

Pakistan will be very disappointed with the way India took the game away. They should have closed the innings pretty early but the carnage from the lower order has taken the game slightly away and now what could have been an easy chase will be a real pressure work fom them. Pakistan Women used five bowlers only and each got a wicket to their name but Nashra Sandhu was the pick with good economy and two wickets claimed.

A story of two halves for India. First, it was the partnership at the top between Smriti Mandhana and Deepti Sharma of 92 runs and then we saw a middle order collapse and then another brilliant partnership. At one stage India were looking down the barrel but the alliance of Sneh Rana and Pooja Vastrakar was a breath of fresh air. It was not a lower order execution but some proper cricketing shots from both the players. They scored boundaries, pierced through the gaps and played extraordinarily well to pull back India from a very bad position. After the wicket of Raj, no one expected anything in excess of 200 but Rana and Pooja showed intent in their batting.

Excellent recovery from India Women! They were in all sorts of trouble at 114/6 but a partnership of 122 runs between Pooja Vastrakar and Sneh Rana has made sure that they post a competitive total on the board. 200 never looked on the cards at one stage but these two have done incredibly well to get India to a defendable total.

FOUR! STREAKY! That spoils a good over! A full toss, on middle. Jhulan Goswami skips down to slog but she gets an inside edge which runs past the short fine leg fielder for a boundary. India Women end with 244/7.
A full ball, on middle. Sneh Rana skips down and drags it back past the bowler towards long on for a single.
A half-volley, oustide off. Jhulan Goswami drills it to long off for a single.
A full ball, outside off. Sneh Rana shuffles across to scoop but she miscues it towards the square leg region. A single taken.

OUT! BOWLED! Fatima Sana gets the prized scalp of Pooja Vastrakar but the damage has already been done! A length ball, around middle. Pooja Vastrakar looks to heave it across the line but she misses and the ball cannons onto her stumps. End of a brilliant knock from Vastrakar!

Four! That is a great shot. Short in length, the battercuts it through square leg and finds the boundary.
Four! Good ball but a good shot too. This is the wrong ‘un but the batterhas picked it. Reverse sweeps it through square leg.
1 run, that is pulled away, through the mid on, for a single.
Four! That is pulled through the on side. The ball races to the fence in no time.
1 run, the on drive comes out now. The battergets a run.
No run, the batter cuts the ball square but it is intercepted.
A full ball, on middle. Sneh Rana skips down and heaves it across the line towards mid-wicket for a run.
No run, that is punched off the back foot, but not in the gap.
2 runs, innovative shot. The reverse sweep comes out and the batterhelps himself to a couple.
There is some technical issue with the stream. Apologizes for the inconvenience caused. Please bear with us...
Another ball, full and on middle. Sneh Rana drags it to mid-wicket for one run.

A length ball, on middle. Pooja Vastrakar gets an inside edge onto her pad as she tries to slog. The ball rolls away to the leg side for a single. 100-run partnership between Pooja Vastrakar and Sneh Rana! This is the first 100-run partnership for the 7th wicket in the history of ICC Women's World Cup.

Back of a length, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar guides it behind square on the off side for a couple of runs. FIFTY on World Cup debut for Pooja Vastrakar! She deserves each and every applause she is getting at the ground.
An overpitched ball, on middle. Sneh Rana looks to slog but gets the toe end of the bat and onto the deck.
A full ball, on middle. Sneh Rana sweeps it in front of square and comes back for the second run.
Fuller in length, on middle, worked to long on for a single.
On a length, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar blocks it to point.

Tossed up, outside off. Sneh Rana keeps it out.
FOUR! CRUNCHED! A short ball, outside off. Sneh Rana cuts hard and the fielder at extra cover misfields. The ball races away to the fence.
On a length, around off. Pooja Vastrakar eases it to long on for a run.

A loopy ball, on middle. Sneh Rana sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a run.

Another ball, full and outside off. Sneh Rana carves it through the extra cover region but manages only a run.

A yorker-length ball, on middle. Pooja Vastrakar digs it out towards long on for a single.
Full and outside off. Pooja Vastrakar drives but straight to the cover fielder.
A slower ball, on a length, around off. Pooja Vastrakar hangs back and looks to flick but she gets an inside edge onto her pad.
Good-length ball, around off. Pooja Vastrakar defends it to cover.
A length ball, angling down leg. Pooja Vastrakar turns it behind square on the leg side and retains the strike by taking a single.
Flatter ball, around middle. Pooja Vastrakar gets forward and keeps it out.

Flatter and quicker, on middle. Pooja Vastrakar rocks back and flat-bats it towards long on for a single.
Flatter and quicker, on middle. Sneh Rana nudges it to the leg side for a run.
A loopy ball, on middle. Sneh Rana paddles it through the fine leg region for a couple of runs.
Another ball, full and outside off. Pooja Vastrakar carves it through the cover region for a brace.
A full ball, outside off. Sneh Rana drives it past the cover fielder and the batters collect three runs.

A slower ball, full and on off. Sneh Rana reads it, prods and blocks it watchfully.
FOUR! WHACKED! A juicy full toss, on middle. Sneh Rana heaves it through the vacant mid-wicket region and bags a boundary.

A full ball, on middle. Sneh Rana heaves it behind square on the leg side and the batters do well to take three runs in total.
On a length, around middle. Pooja Vastrakar eases it to long on for a run.
A low full toss, on middle. Sneh Rana drags it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Deft touch! Back of a length, outside off. Sneh Rana stays back and just guides it past the diving keeper and the ball races away to the third man fence. That also brings up the 50-run partnership between Rana and Vastrakar!
End of Powerplay 2! Pakistan Women can now have a maximum of 5 fielders outside the ring till the 50th over!
Short ball, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar punches off the back foot, through point for a brace. What an innings this is from her.
Short and outside off, cut away to deep point for one.
A full ball, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar comes down the track and looks to go big but slices it to point where the catch is taken. It was a no ball means just a single.

Short of a length, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar miscues her pulls it to mid off.

On a length, outside off, worked to point.

Wide! A length ball, down the leg side. Pooja Vastrakar shoulders arms to it.
On a length, on middle. Blocked out.
Short again, outside off but this time there is a fielder at sweeper cover. A single taken.
Short again, on middle, pulled to short fine leg.
FOUR! Anything short and that is dispatched! Short ball, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar goes back in her crease and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Outside off. Pooja Vastrakar plays it late to short third man.

Wide! Arm ball again, straying down the leg side. Rana misses her sweep.

On middle, Rana works it to mid-wicket for a single.

Good work from these two. Not getting in shell and keeping themselves busy by taking singles. Length ball, outside off. Rana drops it to point for one.
On a length, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar dabs it to short third man for a quick single.
Diana Baig (5-1-17-1) is back into the attack.
On middle, it is hit to mid-wicket for a single.

Full and outside off, driven to mid off.

Tossed up, on off. Pooja tucks it to mid-wicket for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! How big is this wicket? Just in the context of the game! Everything was dependant on her but now she too goes back with a cheap score. India really looking down the barrel now. This is full and outside off. Raj steps down and tries to go big on the leg side but it takes the splice of the bat and goes towards point where Diana Baig takes a simple catch. Pakistan Women are bossing this game at the moment!
Commentary.Howout: c Diana Baig b Nashra Sandhu

Sneh Rana walks out to bat.

Review time! Harmanpreet Kaur takes the LBW decision upstairs. A little murmur when the ball passes the bat but the third umpire says no bat involved. Three reds on Ball Tracker and Harmanpreet Kaur takes the review along with her.

OUT! LBW! India Women lose another wicket and this is a huge one in the context of the game! Pakistan's vice-captain gets rid of India's vice-captain! Nida Dar appeals and the umpire agrees. Harmanpreet Kaur opts for a review. Nothing on the UltraEdge. The Ball Tracker indicates three reds and Kaur is a goner. India Women lose a review as well.

This is tossed up, on off. Smriti Mandhana skips down and looks to push it towards long off but ends up chipping it straight back to the bowler. Anam Amin takes a simple catch. Huge blow this for India Women as another set batter makes her way back.

OUT! BOWLED! Nashra Sandhu strikes and this is a much-needed breakthrough for Pakistan Women! Nashra Sandhu serves a length ball, just outside off that spins in late. Deepti Sharma gets on her knee and shuffles across to sweep but she misses it completely and the ball cannons onto her off stump. India Women lose their second wicket. She shuffled too much there and the ball was too short as well to sweep actually.

Floated, full and on off. Smriti Mandhana skips down the track and eases it to long off for a run. 25th ODI FIFTY for Smriti Mandhana! Wonderful knock. She was under some pressure but started to up the ante as the game progressed. She will eye for three digits now.

Shorter and outside off. Mandhana dabs it past short third man. Sharma calls for two and they get it easily.
Tossed up, on middle. Mandhana comes down the pitch and blocks it out.
A flighted ball, on middle. Smriti prods to defend.
FOUR! Runs flowing nicely now! Full ball, slanting down the leg side and Mandhana sweeps it late to fine leg for a boundary.
Tossed up, on middle. Sharma sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.
Wide! Flatter and angling down the leg side. Left alone.
Fuller and on off. Mandhana steps across and defends it to mid off.
A length ball, outside off. Deepti opens the face of the bat and guides it to third man for one.
This is slapped straight to point.
Length ball, outside off, this is hit to cover-point.
FOUR! Good shot! A full ball, outside off. Sharma gets low, whips it with the bottom hand to mid-wicket for a boundary.
A length ball, outside off, Sharma chops it to point.
End of Powerplay 1! Pakistan Women can now have a maximum of 4 fielders outside the inner circle till the 40th over. Also, Fatima Sana comes to bowl now.
SIX! BANG! Gets hold off this one! A loopy ball, on a length, around middle. Smriti Mandhana shimmies down the track and smacks it over long off for a biggie.
A quicker ball, around off and turning away late. Smriti Mandhana keeps it out.

This is tossed up, on middle. Smriti Mandhana skips down the track and looks to go over long on but doesn't time it well and the ball goes high in the air and lands just in front of the ropes. The fielder at mid on cuts it off and the batters take two runs.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Deepti Sharma cuts it past the cover fielder for a single.
Tosses it up, on leg. Deepti Sharma sweeps hard but straight to the square leg fielder.
Floated, full and outside off. Deepti Sharma gets forward and pushes it to cover.
Change. Nida Dar is into the attack now.
Still can't find the gap! A full ball, on off. Smriti Mandhana looks to slog but it goes off the inner half of the bat towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Short of a length, outside off. Smriti Mandhana hangs back and punches it towards the cover-point fielder.
Hammered but for no run! Fuller in length, outside off. Smriti Mandhana drives but Bismah Maroof at cover, dives to her right and stops a certain boundary.
On a length, around middle. Smriti Mandhana blocks it off the back foot.
Drop and run! Back of a length, around off. Deepti Sharma taps it towards backward point and rotates the strike.
A full ball, outside off. Deepti Sharma drives it past the diving fielder at cover for a couple of runs.
A loopy ball, outside off. Smriti Mandhana tries to cut but she misses.
A short ball, outside off. Smriti Mandhana stays back, opens the face of her bat and guides it past the short third man fielder for a brace.
This is darted on the pads. Deepti Sharma tucks it wide of mid on for a quick single.

Shouts of catch it but the ball lands safely! Floated, full and outside off. Smriti Mandhana looks to heave it across the line but it goes off the bottom half of the blade, in the air and just over the extra cover fielder. A single taken.
Shorter in length, outside off. Smriti Mandhana cuts it to the fielder at cover-point.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Smriti Mandhana punches it towards cover.
Good-length ball, on middle. Deepti Sharma blocks it off the back foot. A maiden over from Baig!
Fuller in length, outside off. Deepti Sharma drives but finds the cover fielder. This must be quite frustrating for India Women.
On a length, around middle. Deepti Sharma keeps it out.
Back of a length, on off. Deepti Sharma taps it to the off side and looks for a run but is sent back by Mandhana.
Good-length ball, around off. Deepti Sharma covers the line and blocks it out.
A length ball, around middle. Deepti Sharma stays back and tucks it to square leg.
Can't find the gap this time around as well! A short ball, outside off. Smriti Mandhana rocks back and slaps it towards the cover-point fielder.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Smriti Mandhana cuts hard but straight to the cover-point fielder.
On a length, outside off. Deepti Sharma shuffles across and nudges it to the leg side for a run.
Sloppy from Pakistan Women! A flatter ball, outside off. Smriti Mandhana punches it towards cover where the fielder fumbles and concedes a single.
Floated, on a length, outside off. Smriti Mandhana hangs back and punches it to cover.
A loopy ball, on off. Smriti Mandhana gets forward and pushes it towards mid on.
On a length, on the pads. Sharma helps it to the fine leg region and longer boundaries there means she get a couple of runs.
Fuller and on middle. Mandhana gently taps it to mid on and takes off for a quick single. Makes to the other end on time.
Just two runs! Short and on middle. Mandhana gets a top edge as she looks to hook it, over the keeper and for a brace.
NO BALL! A length ball, inswinger, around off. Mandhana defends it out. A late no ball as Baig overstepped and Mandhana has a chance to go big.
Pitches it up, on off. Smriti keeps it out on the leg side.
Angles a full ball, from 'round the wicket on middle. Blocked out.
FOUR! First boundary and it comes from the blade of the elegant player! A length ball, on middle. Mandhana flicks it nicely through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short ball, outside off. Left alone.
Amin gives air this time, floated, full and on off. Sharma on the front foot, defends it.
Tossed up, on middle. Mandhana works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Another solid block from Mandhana.
Shorter ball, on off. Smriti Mandhana defends it out.
Flatter and on off. Blocked out.

OUT! BOWLED! Superb start from Pakistan Women! Diana Baig gives them an early reward. They are pumped up and why not because Shafali Verma could have been very lethal up the order. This is full and around off, it lands and nips back in a touch. Verma stays back and without any foot movement swings across the line but the ball movement beats the inside edge and rattles the stumps. Shafali Verma goes back without opening her account.
Deepti Sharma walks out to the middle.
Wide! A full ball, down the leg side. Verma leaves it alone.
Full ball, outward movement, on off, Verma drills it to mid off.
Touch fuller, on middle, pushed to mid on.
A full toss, on the pads, flicked to the left of mid-wicket but a good fielding there does not allow Verma to get underway.
BEATEN! A full ball, outside off and swinging away as well. Verma chases as she looks to drive but misses.
On a length, outside off. Verma punches it to covers.
Maiden to start for Anam Amin! Tossed up, on off. Mandhana blocks it out. Good start by Pakistan Women.
Spin there as this one comes back in, on middle, Mandhana knocks it to covers.
This one skids through, full ball and Smriti defends it.
Flatter this time, outside off. Mandhana cuts it on the back foot, but straight to the fielder at point.
Tossed up, full and around off, Mandhana keeps it out.
Floated full and on off. Mandhana watchfully pushes it to point.
Who will bowl from the other end? Anam Amin it is.
A full toss, around off, pushed to the right of mid off and Mandhana will keep the strike.
Beaten! A length ball, angling outside off. Smriti looks to drive on the up but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Good shape there! A length ball, inswinger this time, on middle. Mandhana on her back foot, blocks it out.
A full toss, on off, pushed to mid off.
India are underway! Fuller ball, outside off, hint of away swing. Mandhana looks to drive but it goes off the splice to third man for a couple of runs.
Baig starts with a length ball, around off. Mandhana steps across and pushes it to covers.

We are done with all the pre-match formalities and it is time for live action! The players have made their way out to the middle. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana to open the batting for India Women. Diana Baig will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
The match officials and the players have lined up for the national anthems. The anthem of India will be played first, followed by the anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain is near the pitch. He says that this is a used pitch but it looks good to bat on. Tells that there is not a lot of grass on the pitch and the batters will enjoy batting on it.

Bismah Maroof, the skipper of Pakistan Women, says they would have bowled first because the wicket looks damp. Adds, they are going with five bowlers and they have prepared well, just need to believe in themselves. She is blessed to be back.

Mithali Raj, the skipper of India Women, says that they will bat first. Tells that this is a good pitch to bat on and they will look to put up a good score on the board. Mentions that they took a lot of positives from the ODI series against New Zealand. Informs that they are going with three pacers and three spinners.
Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Bismah Maroof (C), Sidra Ameen, Javeria Khan, Omaima Sohail, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Fatima Sana, Sidra Nawaz (WK), Diana Baig, Nashra Sandhu, Anam Amin.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Deepti Sharma, Harmanpreet Kaur, Mithali Raj (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Sneh Rana, Jhulan Goswami, Meghna Singh, Pooja Vastrakar, Rajeshwari Gayakwad.
TOSS - India Women have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first!

Pakistan Women haven't had the best of times previously in this mega-event and Bismah Maroof would be itching to turn the tables this time around. They have some talented youngsters in their lineup but also have the experience of Bismah Maroof and Javeria Khan. Will Pakistan Women be able to draw first blood and register a win? We'll find that soon. Stay tuned for toss and team news.

Both India Women and Pakistan Women will be playing their first game of the tournament and they would be eager to start off on a winning note. India Women have had their dominance over Pakistan Women, especially in this format and Mithali and her troops would be confident going into this clash. They are yet to lose an ODI against Pakistan Women and would be keen to hand them a defeat yet again. This might be the last chance for the veteran duo of Mithali Raj and Jhulan Goswami to give a shot at this prestigious trophy. And after that 2017 underdogs story, India would like to place the final jigsaw this time.

Hello and a very warm welcome to the coverage of one of the most awaited clashes of the ICC Women's World Cup, 2022. Mithali Raj-led India Women will take on Bismah Maroof-led Pakistan Women and we are in for an intriguing contest as two Asian giants go head-to-head at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui.
